Looks like there is an app you can download too that can do stuff like scanning for tags nearby.
Thank you - the tracker they use weighs in at 60 milligrams, incredibly light.

What is unclear to me is whether a special phone app is required or not. One of the web pages indicates that it piggybacks onto the infrastructure for airtags/android tags (not clear which). Certainly, if I was building these, that is what I would do as getting a custom app in enough phones would be extremely difficult.

Having said that, the claim is also that these tags report temperature as well — but there is a field (personalized name) that could be used to transport that information. In any case, it is an impressively small tracker!

An app for tracking monarchs with these tags is here for iOS [1].

[1] https://apps.apple.com/us/app/project-monarch-science/id6460...
I've moved some of those links to the toptext. Thanks!

The site looks like it got hugged to death.

I’m on the monarch migration path and had wild milkweeds with monarch butterflies for a few years but the last 2-3 years oleander aphids exploded in population and I’ve seen a single caterpillar since.

Are there ways to mitigate that while not killing the monarchs or am I just shit out of luck?
I release ladybugs every year and that seems to help.  You can buy them online if they are hard to find locally.
The ones available online are from the western U.S.; depending on where you live, that may be counterproductive to the locally native species that are struggling.

Grow some yarrow, dill, or sunflowers and get ladybugs to lay their eggs all over your garden naturally, and I imagine you'll start to see much better results! Larval stage ladybugs are significantly more ravenous than their adult forms.
